correctness.rationale: The digit language partitions all accepted indices. The exact least-lexicographic valid carry proves the successor formula for all inputs, including the all-ones boundary. Exact tiling bijections count every terminal class. Primitivity of the tiling automaton and prefix-subtree decomposition prove relative frequencies for arbitrary cutoffs; modular wraparound establishes the sole duplicate gap. Standalone finite checker reproduces predicted small cases; no finite tests serve as infinite proof.

evidence: Merta proves unbounded zero runs and at most two adjacent ones, without classifying individual zero-run lengths.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The structurally strongest same-family prior results have nonidentical claims and do not imply exact return-gap frequencies of one-positions. The present all-r distribution cannot be obtained just from the cited upper run bound, parity, or nonregularity results.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither the same-family lower-level statements nor the other invariant results entail the complete successor, exact multiplicity and all-cutoff limiting-frequency assertions. A formal calculation is given rather than claiming novelty from unsuccessful searches.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The equivalent enumerator and regular digit-language descriptions have been examined, not merely their titles. They specify the indices but do not themselves state the exact successor gap-spectrum, all-r shell multiplicities or normalized limiting frequencies. A derivation from the language is supplied as the new result.

evidence: A060142 provides initial terms and recursive generation, including their relation to the ordinary Baum–Sweet sequence.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The inspected entry is a table of index values, not a table or exact formula of the all-order gaps and frequency measures. No direct exact target invariant was located. An unindexed or distinct entry remains a risk.

originality.rationale: Theorem statements and implications were compared to the source that defines the exact generalized word family and proves closest run/one-index properties. In particular, Merta’s apparent gap theorem concerns formal-inverse positions rather than one-positions. The other direct same-word article computes opacity, while the OEIS entry gives an index table but not the exact all-r return-gap spectrum or law. An unindexed equivalent remains a stated risk, not proof of absolute uniqueness.
residual_risks: An equivalent result might appear in an unindexed combinatorics-on-words or integer-sequences source.
The OEIS database could have a different sequence entry for special-case gaps not linked from the inspected one.

value.rationale: For every generalized Baum–Sweet family member, the theorem determines a natural complete recurrence-time invariant (all attainable gaps), exact counts in every binary shell, and a nondegenerate probabilistic return law despite the one-symbol density being zero. This information is not a routine reformulation of an upper bound on consecutive symbols; it is a full structural classification valuable for automatic-word recurrence statistics.
